items.title: New Cyberpunk 2077 Sale Brings the Ultimate Edition to Its Lowest Price Ever
items.summary: Pick up Cyberpunk 2077 and its Phantom Liberty expansion for cheaper than ever before in a sale on one platform.
items.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook A new sale for Cyberpunk 2077 has brought the Ultimate Edition of the game to its lowest price ever. With the arrival of the Phantom Liberty expansion for Cyberpunk 2077 back in 2023, CD Projekt Red released an Ultimate Edition of its first-person RPG that included all of the game’s content in a single package. Since then, this has been the definitive version of Cyberpunk 2077 to buy for those who haven’t yet picked up the title. And while countless millions have since bought Cyberpunk 2077 for themselves, a new offer may be too good to pass up for those who have remained on the fence.

As of this week, Cyberpunk 2077: Ultimate Edition has seen its value cut all the way down to $27.99. This represents a discount of over $40, as the game normally retails for $69.99. The deal, which is set to last until November 3rd, represents the lowest amount that the Ultimate Edition of Cyberpunk 2077 has ever sold for, making this the most notable discount in the game’s history.

The downside with this deal is that it doesn’t apply to all versions of Cyberpunk 2077 . Instead, the sale is only live on the Nintendo eShop for the Switch 2 edition of the game. As a result, those on PS5, Xbox Series X/S, and PC platforms can’t get Cyberpunk 2077: Ultimate Edition for the same low price.

While this might be a disappointment, it’s still impressive that Cyberpunk 2077 is this cheap on Switch 2 to begin with. The Switch 2 version of the game is technically the newest one that has been released, as it just launched in tandem with the new Nintendo hardware last year. As such, for its price to have been cut by this much is quite impressive given that the Ultimate Edition has never been as low on the PlayStation Store, Xbox Store, or Steam.

Fortunately, for those looking to pick up Cyberpunk 2077: Ultimate Edition on other platforms, similar offers are currently ongoing. The Ultimate Edition on Steam is now down to $33.10, while the Xbox Store is only a bit more costly at $31.99. A similar sale has yet to kick in on the PS Store, but it likely will in the days to come.

As for the reason behind these sales, it almost certainly has to do with the arrival of Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2 this week . The new release in the hugely popular anime series is driving greater interest in Cyberpunk as a whole, which has prompted CDPR to discount the game to take advantage. So if you end up watching Edgerunners 2 for yourself and want to snag the Ultimate Edition , now would definitely be the best time to do so.

items.title: Cyberpunk 2077 Co-Op Multiplayer Is Coming
items.content:
Cyberpunk 2077 game cover By Tom Wilson Published Oct 19, 2026, 3:00 PM EDT Tom Wilson is a Gaming Features Writer at Screen Rant. Over the past five years, Tom has worked as the Editor-in-Chief at The Game Crater, as a Staff Writer for GamingIntel, a List Writer at TheGamer, and, of course, as a Senior Writer at ScreenRant. Tom has experience writing reviews, guides, news, and features, and has been responsible for teams of writers, training them and editing their work. Tom graduated with a Masters in Multimedia Journalism, and has since gone on to build up his portfolio of games journalism work. Sign in to your ScreenRant account Add Us Add on Google Preferred Source Google Discover Summary Generate a summary of this story Like Like follow Follow followed Followed Listen Thread Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap Cyberpunk 2077 is an exceptional RPG, its sprawling, neon-soaked, open-world metropolis providing ample opportunities for role-playing, chaotic carnage, and fun. However, as much fun as it is to roam around Night City alone, one cannot deny that playing alongside a friend would be significantly better. After all, as the adage goes, everything is better with a friend. Grand Theft Auto 5 proved that co-op and competitive multiplayer worked in a roleplay-heavy open-world setting, and it felt only right that Cyberpunk 2077 would follow suit.

However, it never did, with Cyberpunk 2077's official multiplayer mode being canceled , and fans having to toil away in Night City as a lone wolf, forever. It was a sad fate we'd all resigned ourselves to until recently, as a brand-new co-op multiplayer mode is finally coming to Cyberpunk 2077 after all these years, promising fans a truly memorable experience and an all-new way of playing the game. Indeed, this new co-op mode offers fans a whole new perspective on not just Night City, but Cyberpunk 2077 as a whole.

With Cyberpunk 2077's official multiplayer experience ending up being an arcade cabinet for two players, it meant that fans had to deliver the promised experience themselves. Naturally, this has led to mods like Cyber_MP , which allow players to roam around Night City together, wreaking havoc. However, while this is a lot of fun, it doesn't allow you to experience the entire campaign alongside a friend, something that numerous first-person open-world titles such as Far Cry do.

Fortunately, NightCoop , the latest Cyberpunk 2077 mod, completely transforms the game's core campaign to cater to two players. It syncs up the host's save, including NPCs, quests, and the world, with the second player, ensuring that both experience every event, line of dialogue, and set piece simultaneously. Each and every facet of Cyberpunk 2077's design has been carefully considered and tweaked accordingly, including allowing players to vote on each choice (including timed ones), thus including the second player in any meaningful decisions.

It's rather staggering just how robust a mod NightCoop is, how completely and unintrusively it transforms the core Cyberpunk 2077 experience to fully integrate co-operative gameplay. NightCoop goes beyond being a simple Cyberpunk 2077 multiplayer mod ; its ambitions are set far higher than merely offering chaos in Night City alongside a buddy. Being able to fully experience the campaign with a friend affords dedicated fans an entirely new perspective on a story, world, and characters they've become so intimately familiar with. It also adds PvP for those eager to kill their friends, making it the complete package.

NightCoop isn't out yet, but it is well into development, with its developers showcasing new trailers and updates via its official YouTube channel . An Open Beta is starting on Friday, October 23, 2026, and is available for download via the game's official Discord. However, there isn't an ETA for the full project. One can only imagine the work that must go into ensuring every choice, quest, and line of dialogue works, even if only a little, with two players present. Hopefully NightCoop will drop sooner rather than later, as Cyberpunk 2077 is very much in need of a co-op mode.

items.title: Hideo Kojima Confirmed to Reprise Cyberpunk 2077 Role in Edgerunners 2 Anime Cameo
items.summary: Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2 has cast Metal Gear Solid creator Hideo Kojima in a role that will see him reprise his part from Cyberpunk 2077.
items.content:
Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2 has cast Metal Gear Solid creator Hideo Kojima in a role that will see him reprise his part from Cyberpunk 2077 .

Series game developer CD Projekt Red confirmed the news in a social media post on X/Twitter . The message teased that it's more than a throwaway part, too, as Kojima will be seen playing "the famous braindance director who was at Konpeki Plaza in Cyberpunk 2077" (via X's machine translation).

The real-life game director was quick to respond and share his excitement, as well as a few pictures from his time recording his lines. His full statement, minus a few fun emojis, is as follows: "I make a cameo appearance in the anime series Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2 as Hideyoshi Oshima, the character who appeared in the previous game."

I make a cameo appearance in the anime series “Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2” as Hideyoshi Oshima, the character who appeared in the previous game. 🙏🙇🏻😅🫶👍 https://t.co/OuUaazFfR4

Cyberpunk 2077 players were treated to an unexpected visit from the Kojima Productions lead when they first traveled to Night City back in 2020. It's a moment that wasn't actually directly tied to V's mainline quest and surprisingly easy to miss, but yes, if players search Arasaka's Konpeki Plaza hard enough, they can find Kojima sitting near a bar.

If you're familiar with Kojima's work on games like Metal Gear Solid and Death Stranding, what he had to say in the Cyberpunk world wasn't too surprising. He enjoyed chatting about the in-universe memory-exploring mechanic, braindances, as he wanted his "productions to convey real, raw human emotion." When stopped by V, he asks the player if they have any pitches to show him.

"The feeling when you combine happiness and melancholy, or being calm with an underlying sense of anxiety," he says in the game. "These complex, realistic feelings and emotions are what I aspire to recreate... woven into much better stories, of course."

Kojima's Oshima will now bring his love for braindance technology to Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2 when it premieres tomorrow, October 20, 2026. All 10 episodes of the second season will drop at the same time. IGN called this second anime trip into Night City "Amazing" in our 9/10 review .

"Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2 delivers the gory, action-packed goods, even if it doesn’t quite hit the highs of its predecessor,” we said.

Kojima is hard at work on games like Physint and OD , but that doesn't mean he hasn't had time for one or even a few cameos. We know now that Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2 was one of the few anime projects he teased earlier this month, but we're still waiting to see the "big movie" he filmed .

Returning to Cyberpunk 2077 or playing it for the first time? We’ve got a new and improved Cyberpunk interactive map to help you find every mission, Iconic item, and collectible in the game. Plus, we’ve also got a full walkthrough for the base game, a Phantom Liberty walkthrough , and an overview of all the Cyberpunk 2077 endings so you don’t make a choice you regret. And we can’t ignore the various romance options you can smooch, which also impact how V’s story concludes.

Michael Cripe is a freelance writer with IGN. He's best known for his work at sites like The Pitch, The Escapist, and OnlySP. Be sure to give him a follow on Bluesky (@mikecripe.bsky.social) and Twitter (@MikeCripe).

items.summary: Kojima will reprise his role as braindance producer Hideyoshi Oshima…
items.content:
Kojima will reprise his role as braindance producer Hideyoshi Oshima

Video Game News 19th Oct 2026 / 1:23 pm Posted by Chris Scullion Hideo Kojima will appear in the Cyberpunk 2077 universe for the second time, it’s been confirmed.

The Death Stranding [325 articles]" href=https://www.videogameschronicle.com/games/death-stranding/ >Death Stranding and Metal Gear creator will appear in the second season of Cyberpunk: Edgerunners, which is set to start on Netflix [417 articles]" href=https://www.videogameschronicle.com/companies/netflix/ >Netflix this Tuesday, October 20.

Kojima first made a cameo appearance in the main Cyberpunk 2077 [550 articles]" href=https://www.videogameschronicle.com/games/cyberpunk-2077/ >Cyberpunk 2077 game itself, where he appeared as the similarly-named Hideyoshi Oshima.

Kojima’s character Oshima can be seen during the mission The Heist, if the player makes the decision to look around the hotel bar. He’s sitting at a table at the back, talking to people about his work.

Oshima is a producer of ‘braindance’, a technology in Cyberpunk 2077 that lets people record their experiences and play back someone else’s including not just what they see and hear but also what they smell, touch and taste, as well as their emotions and thoughts.

Now he’ll be making a return in Cyberpunk: Edgerunners Season 2, where he’ll once again be voiced by Kojima.

Spotting a familiar face, chooms? 👀 You may remember seeing him in Konpeki Plaza during The Heist in 2077. Now, the renowned braindance director is making another appearance in Night City. @HIDEO_KOJIMA_EN returns as Hideyoshi Oshima in Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2! pic.twitter.com/2Mt0RBapqw

Kojima’s appearance in the Cyberpunk universe has more meaning to it than some may realise. Before his work became hugely popular with the Metal Gear Solid series, Kojima created a cyberpunk-themed visual novel which enjoys cult classic status to this day.

Snatcher was originally released on the PC [13,111 articles]" href=https://www.videogameschronicle.com/platforms/pc/ >PC -8801 and MSX2 computers in Japan in 1988, before coming to the Sega [1,216 articles]" href=https://www.videogameschronicle.com/companies/sega/ >Sega CD / Mega CD, PC-Engine Super CD-ROM2, PlayStation [12,757 articles]" href=https://www.videogameschronicle.com/platforms/playstation/ >PlayStation and Saturn in the 1990s. The only version which got an English language release was the Sega CD / Mega CD one.

items.title: Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2 Includes The Return Of An Iconic Developer
items.summary: The same developer who made an appearance in Cyberpunk 2077.
items.content:
CD Projekt/Netflix By Josh Coulson Published Oct 19, 2026, 6:05 AM EDT Josh Coulson is an editor at TheGamer covering breaking news on everything from colorful platformers to the latest Lego sets. Primarily a news writer since 2018, Josh has covered just about every major game from the past decade. Now an editor, their focus has shifted to being the leading affiliate expert at the site, building relationships between TheGamer and global brands including Mattel, Funko, and The Pokemon Company. Sign in to your TheGamer account Add Us Summary Generate a summary of this story Like Like follow Follow followed Followed Thread Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap The wait between Cyberpunk 2077 and its sequel is going to be a long one, but fans of the CD Projekt series can return to Night City tomorrow as Edgerunners season two arrives on Netflix. They might notice a familiar face from not just Cyberpunk, but the wider games industry, as the reveal that Hideo Kojima is making his debut in the show has been announced ahead of time.

Kojima’s return to Night City in the upcoming season of Edgerunners was revealed via the show’s Twitter account. “Spotting a familiar face, chooms? You may remember seeing him in Konpeki Plaza during The Heist in 2077. Now, the renowned braindance director is making another appearance in Night City,” the post confirming the Metal Gear Solid creator’s Cyberpunk return reads.

The post also shows a glimpse of what Kojima looks like in Edgerunners’ reimagined anime Cyberpunk world, since the only form we’ve seen him in so far in Night City was in-game courtesy of his cameo in Cyberpunk 2077. Just how extensive Kojima’s role will be in Edgerunners 2 hasn’t been revealed.

As noted in the Edgerunners post, Hideyoshi Koshima, Kojima’s character in Cyberpunk, can be found in Konpeki Plaza. The character is a braindance producer, and his wants and goals for the fictional futuristic medium are much the same as Kojima’s approach to game development. Oshima doesn’t just want to give people the best and deepest braindance experiences - he strives for every new product he makes to provide new personal connections unlike any achieved in the braindance genre before them.

Basically, Oshima’s products are to braindance what Kojima hoped Death Stranding would be to video games. Speaking of which, Cyberpunk 2077 also includes a Death Stranding easter egg in the form of a bridge baby pod. It seems unlikely that will be joining Oshima in the new season of Edgerunners, but you never know.

Oshima means big island, while Kojima means little island, which is a neat detail I just learned courtesy of the Cyberpunk Wiki .

Oshima might well be one of the only characters we recognize when Edgerunners 2 arrives on Netflix tomorrow. Its creators have said since season one that, if there were ever a season two, it would tell an entirely different story using brand new characters. Edgerunners 2 will fulfill that promise. The new season tells a new story, and while it takes place in the same city as the game and the first season, we’re about to finally be properly introduced to even more Cyberpunk characters we will all inevitably fall in love with over the next few days.

items.title: Cyberpunk 2077 free mod restores 2,200 NPCs to Night City
items.summary: Night City has never been more vibrant!
items.content:
Over 2,200 unused NPCs have been restored in Night City

Night City in Cyberpunk 2077 feels more alive than ever with this free mod, making CD Projekt RED's RPG even more immersive. Hopefully, that should help pass the time until Project Orion , the Cyberpunk 2077 sequel.

From the creators of The Witcher series, CD Projekt RED 's Cyberpunk 2077 is now considered one of the greatest sci-fi RPGs of all time, and rightly so; it's a fantastic experience.

We all remember Cyberpunk 2077's rocky launch, which was so bad that it was removed from the PlayStation Store for around six months. Credit to CD Projekt RED, though, for fixing its bugs and adding missing features, with many fans now feeling the game has exceeded expectations. However, one area where Night City could still improve is the density and variety of its population. Thankfully, this free mod fixes that.

The mod is called Crowd Variety Restored , was created by dnbnhlp, and is free to download right now via Nexus Mods. It does exactly what you'd expect, but perhaps a little bit more, and we'll take you through its best features right here.

This mod makes Night City feel more immersive and alive. One of the gripes many players have with huge open worlds is that we regularly see the same NPCs littered all over the map. This mod corrects that by restoring NPC appearances that were removed from the game's launch, for whatever reason.

“Ever notice the same junkie on every corner? In vanilla Night City, she has exactly two looks. The homeless guy with the backpack has three, and nonbinary corpo women share just three between them. No wonder you keep seeing the same faces in different places,” reads the mod's description.

“Yet CDPR made over 2,200 extra crowd looks, finished them, shipped them with the game, and then never let them reach the streets. New colours, new hair, new jewellery, and whole outfits have been sitting in the game files all along. This mod brings them back.”

Of course, the best feature of this mod is the restoration of more than 2,200 unused NPC appearances discovered in the game files.

Not only does this mod reportedly double the variety of civilian NPCs, but more than 90% of civilian types receive additional appearance options, making the crowds feel less repetitive.

NPCs now have a greater variety of hairstyles, hair colours and clothing, adding more diversity to Night City's population.

Alongside the extra clothing and hairstyles, NPCs in Night City will have more cyberware augmentations and accessories.

The NPCs labelled as “junkie women” can at least look a little less generic, with 30 different appearances instead of the original two. This includes eight new outfits.

Homeless men with backpacks get 40 different appearances instead of the original three. They'll also have 17 new outfits.

items.title: The ‘Cyberpunk 2077’ Movie Will Expand the Game, Not Adapt It
Cyberpunk 2077's Movie Adaptation Comes With One Controversial Twist
items.summary: The Cyberpunk 2077 movie is going to take a controversial approach to telling its story, and it
items.content:
CD Projekt Red Add SlashFilm on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover Begun, the video game movie wars have. Like the superhero movie boom before it, video game adaptations have suddenly become the hottest ticket in town — and you just know studios are going to do everything they can to take full advantage of this while they can. The newly-merged Paramount/Warner Bros. ( now under the umbrella of Skydance ) is at the top of that list, fast-tracking projects such as the "Sonic the Hedgehog" movies, the recent "Street Fighter," the upcoming "Call of Duty" blockbuster, and more. The next one on the agenda to get the live-action treatment will be "Cyberpunk 2077," the infamously bug-ridden (but, once we got past all that, exceptionally entertaining) 2020 open-world title.

All that we initially knew was that the planned "Cyberpunk" movie would be set in the fictional dystopian town of Night City, but now we're learning new details about what's in store ... and, like practically any other video game-related update these days, it's bound to cause some controversy. In a new interview with Polish outlet PAP Biznes (via Polygon ), CD Projekt Red co-CEO Michał Nowakowski revealed that the video game company has very specific ideas in mind about how they want Paramount and the yet-to-be-revealed creative team to approach this adaptation. According to Nowakowski:

"At this point, we can only say that we definitely don't want to make a film adaptation of the game. We want to tell a story in the world of 'Cyberpunk,' but it won't be a one-to-one translation of the game's story."

CD Projekt Red With respect to all the chooms who were gearing up for Keanu Reeves to reprise his role as the punk-rocker Johnny Silverhand and dreaming about all their fan-casts over who could play main protagonist V, allow us to throw some cold water real quick. Whatever form this movie based on "Cyperpunk 2077" ultimately takes, we now know for sure that it won't be a direct copy-and-paste job of the story from the game ... and we couldn't be more relieved to hear it.

It's the only approach that makes any narrative sense, really. Before anyone starts throwing rotten vegetables at us, that's not to say we aren't hopeful to see characters like V (whatever gender the writers decide on), Johnny, Jackie, or fan-favorites Panam Palmer and Judy Álvarez end up playing some sort of a role in the adaptation. But for a game so dependent on player choices and optionality and alternate endings (not unlike "Mass Effect," which still faces plenty of its own hurdles as a TV adaptation ), how could a movie stripping all that away from viewers ever hope to live up to what the game pulled off so cinematically the first time around? As cutting-edge efforts like "GTA VI" continue to blur the lines between video game graphics and photorealism, live-action adaptations are going to have to work that much harder to justify their own existence.

In other words, perhaps taking the same approach as Zach Cregger's "Resident Evil" is the only way to go. Like Raccoon City, Night City and the surrounding area lend themselves to endless amounts of storytelling possibilities. There's zero reason to give us more of the same ol' stuff when we could get something new and original instead.

items.title: The Cyberpunk 2077 movie won't be 'a film adaptation of the game,' CD Projekt chief says
items.summary: The game is great, but CD Projekt wants to tell a new story.
items.content:
The game is great, but CD Projekt wants to tell a new story.

(Image credit: CDPR) {alert('Link copied')}).catch(err => {console.error('Failed to copy: ', err)})" data-platform="copy_link" data-action="" class="font-ui-heading py-2 text-sm text-neutral-700 hover:bg-neutral-100 transition-colors no-underline block cursor-pointer border-0 bg-transparent w-full text-left normal-case" aria-label="Copy link" role="menuitem" data-analytics-id="article-social" analytics-label="utility-bar-social-share-copy-link" analytics-name="utility-bar-secondary" data-mrf-recirculation="article-social"> Copy link Facebook X Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 6 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter We learned last week that a Cyberpunk 2077 movie is in the works , an announcement I used mainly to talk about a completely different cyberpunk movie starring Keanu Reeves as a guy named Johnny who's having a bad week. Now we've got a bit more insight into what CD Projekt Red has in mind for the film, and it's possible that a guy named Johnny may not be involved at all.

"Our contract with Anonymous Content expired, and in the meantime, an opportunity arose to establish cooperation with Paramount Pictures," co-CEO Michał Nowakowski told Polish PAP Biznes ( Google translated ), referring to the Cyberpunk 2077 "live action project" that was announced in 2023 and ultimately went nowhere. "We decided that we would conduct a live-action Cyberpunk project in a new formula.

"At this point, we can only say that we definitely don't want to make a film adaptation of the game. We want to tell a story in the world of Cyberpunk, but it won't be a one-to-one translation of the game's story."

I loved Cyberpunk 2077, and the fact that it featured two Hollywood stars in central roles might make it seem like a natural fit for a direct translation. But I think avoiding that approach is the wiser move: V's story has been told, and trying to replicate it on film only invites unflattering comparisons and criticism. And it's not as though the world of Night City is short of other stories to tell, after all, nor would it be difficult to indirectly tie it to the game through references or cameos, if the urge to do so is really that strong.

Remember as well that two of the most successful game-to-screen adaptations, Cyberpunk: Edgerunners and Resident Evil , took their respective underlying settings and made them their own. That's basically what Cyberpunk 2077 is, as far as that goes: A vision of Mike Pondsmith's Cyberpunk tabletop setting, interpreted through the lens of a new timeline. They're all stronger for it, because they allow creators to work within a particular framework without tying them to specifics.

items.content:
Patch 2.31 for Cyberpunk 2077 is now live!

This update includes an AutoDrive upgrade and Photo Mode adjustments. It also addresses common issues encountered by players. For details, check the full list of changes below:

Vehicles

  • Updated AutoDrive. When driving to a selected point, the vehicle now drives smoothly, overtakes blocking vehicles and no longer stops at traffic lights. Free Roam mode has also been upgraded to follow traffic rules and navigate the city more reliably.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where Johnny always spawned in the passenger seat when using the Delamain Cab service.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where applying CrystalCoat to the Yaiba ARV-Q340 Semimaru caused its wheels to flash in different colors.

    [/*]

Photo Mode

  • Most of the new poses introduced in Update 2.3 now work with any gender.

    [/*]

  • Disabled NPC collision, which will make it easier to position NPCs on top of other objects with collision (e.g. on car hoods).

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where some of the poses didn't work for Royce.

    [/*]

Quests & Open World

  • Freedom - Fixed the journal entry that appears when the player chooses not to steal the Rayfield Caliburn "Mordred."

    [/*]

  • Motorbreath - Fixed an issue where, after V fails to pursue and stop Semimaru and receives a text from River saying he'll contact V soon, the follow-up message never arrives.

    [/*]

  • Motorbreath - Fixed an issue where the Yaiba Semimaru could flip over during the chase, preventing the player from entering it.

    [/*]

  • Motorbreath - It's no longer possible to trigger the quest if River died during The Hunt.

    [/*]

  • Motorbreath - Players can now acquire the Yaiba ARV-Q340 Semimaru through AUTOFIXER even if they failed The Hunt, which normally unlocks the side quest where the vehicle is obtained.

    [/*]

  • Nitro (Youth Energy) - Fixed a game crash that could occur in certain circumstances after leaving the Yaiba showroom event.

    [/*]

  • Nitro (Youth Energy) - Fixed an issue where the proxy interface UI in the Yaiba showroom is cut off when the "Larger HUD Elements" setting is enabled.

    [/*]

Miscellaneous

  • Fixed several localization and lipsync issues in various languages.

    [/*]

  • Added a toggle to disable vignette. It can be found in Settings → Graphics → Basic.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue on PC and Mac where Ray-Traced Reflections might not display correctly when enabled under certain conditions.

    [/*]

  • Fixed several issues with displaying text messages from Delamain.

    [/*]

  • Various fixes for fluff vendors.

    [/*]

PC-specific

  • Fixed an issue where NVIDIA Reflex could be disabled while DLSS Frame Generation was enabled, causing the screen to turn pink.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where Path Tracing didn't activate properly in certain scenarios.

    [/*]

Mac-specific

  • Fixed an issue where changing graphics presets on Mac set Screen Space Reflections to a higher setting compared to the equivalent presets on PC.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue causing a permanent white screen when Frame Generation is enabled while entering the braindance in The Information.

    [/*]

  • Selecting "Defaults" in Video Settings no longer turns HDR Mode off.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where setting the MetalFX DRS Maximum Resolution above the value applied by the “For this Mac” preset could cause visual artifacts.

    [/*]

  • Fixed the inverted behavior of the "Mute Game in Background" toggle in Settings.

    [/*]

  • Removed the outdated "(Requires Game Restart)" disclaimer from the mouseover description of the "Disable Spatial Audio" setting.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue on the App Store version that caused the game to become stuck on the “Press Space to continue” breaching screen.

    [/*]

  • Various stability and performance optimizations.

    [/*]

Surviving the City of Dreams is tough, but a choom at your side can make all the difference.

In our latest It’s All About You episode, we’re celebrating all of our iconic duos living on the edge! Night City wouldn’t shine quite so bright without them. 

Thank you for staying with us and expressing your love for Cyberpunk: Edgerunners in the most creative ways possible. Don't forget to check out our gallery to see more works, and, of course, share your creations with us: http://cdpred.ly/AAY. See you in the next episode!

items.content:
Update 2.3 lands tomorrow!

Experience Night City in a whole new way — this patch introduces 4 new vehicles, the AutoDrive feature, self-driving Delamain cabs and more! It also contains updates for CrystalCoat™ and Photo Mode, as well as support for AMD FSR 3.1 Frame Generation, Intel XeSS 2.0 and HDR10+ Gaming, among others.

Update 2.3 also brings Cyberpunk 2077 to a whole new platform: Mac with Apple silicon! If you already own the game on Steam, you can play it on your compatible device. To find out whether your Mac can run Cyberpunk 2077, please check the official requirements.

Read the list of changes for more info:

Vehicles

  • Added 4 new vehicles, including several Side Jobs tied to acquiring them:

    • Yaiba ARV-Q340 Semimaru

      Reward from a new side job (to unlock, complete The Hunt and The Beast In Me).

      An additional side job unlocks the CrystalCoat™ feature for it.

      [/*]

    • Rayfield Caliburn "Mordred"

      Reward from a new side job (to unlock, complete The Beast in Me: Badlands, The Beast in Me: Santo Domingo, Transmission, and Search and Destroy)."

      [/*]

    • Yaiba ASM-R250 Muramasa

      Reward from a new side job (to unlock, purchase 1 Yaiba vehicle, purchase at least 3 vehicles through AUTOFIXER, and complete Reported Crime: You Play with Fire...).

      If you fail the side job, the vehicle can later be purchased through AUTOFIXER.

      [/*]

    • Chevillon Legatus 450 Aquila

      Available for purchase on AUTOFIXER.

      [/*]
    [/*]

  • Introducing AutoDrive! This cutting-edge, autonomous driving feature will take you to your chosen destination (i.e. job objective or placed pin on the map). If you have no set destination, it will take you on a leisurely ride through the streets of Night City. Simply hop in any of your vehicles, make sure you're on a road, and hold G (PC) / Left Stick (consoles) to activate. This feature is disabled when you enter combat or when your vehicle is heavily damaged.

    [/*]

  • Implemented Cinematic Camera for AutoDrive. Hold Q (PC) / D-Pad Right (consoles) to activate. Sit back and enjoy cinematic views of Night City as you cruise toward your destination.

    [/*]

  • Self-driving Delamain cabs are now available on demand! Simply open the menu to call vehicles, then select "Delamain Cab" from the list to request a ride. This feature unlocks after completing the job Don't Lose Your Mind (regardless of outcome) and receiving a message from Delamain.

    [/*]

  • Rayfield's CrystalCoat™ is now available for vehicles from partner brands, including motorcycles. Additionally, the infamous hacker known as Cosmetic_Troll exploited a vulnerability and created a cracked version of Rayfield's CrystalCoat™ technology for lower-end vehicles. Please note, however, that some models do not support the technology, such as heavily modded nomad vehicles and job-related vehicles.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where unique color schemes did not work properly on the Mizutani Shion MZ1 and MZ2.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where unique color scheme could not be applied properly to the Villefort Deleon "Vindicator".

    [/*]

Photo Mode

  • Added 27 new NPCs that can be spawned in Photo Mode, including Rita Wheeler, the Cassel twins, fixers, Dum Dum, the iguana, Brendan, and more.

    [/*]

  • You can now switch between alternative outfits for NPCs spawned in Photo Mode.

    [/*]

  • You can now switch between V's saved Wardrobe outfits in Photo Mode.

    [/*]

  • Added a confirmation pop-up when exiting Photo Mode to prevent accidental exits after setting up the perfect shot.

    [/*]

  • Added more customization options to the Look-At Camera feature, including an option for only the character's eyes to turn toward the camera instead of their entire body.

    [/*]

  • Added improvements to Lighting:

    • Lights now spawn around the camera instead of the player character.

      [/*]

    • Added an outline to the spotlight mesh and an indicator when it's off screen for better visibility.

      [/*]

    • Improved light movement speed on controllers.

      [/*]
    [/*]

  • Added multiple new stickers and frames, including iconic quotes and stylish overlays that let you turn your screenshots into Night City postcards – perfect for sharing memories from the City of Dreams.

    [/*]

  • Improved Depth of Field and moved it to the Camera tab.

    [/*]

  • Added a new Color Balance tab, allowing you to create your own custom filters.

    [/*]

  • Added a new Time and Weather tab:

    • Weather: includes rain, acid rain, fog, sandstorm, pollution, and sunny.

      [/*]

    • Time of Day: changes the time of day within Photo Mode.

      [/*]

    • Frame Forward: advances through an unlimited amount of frames to capture the perfect shot.

      [/*]

    • Game Speed: allows in-game time to progress while in Photo Mode."

      [/*]
    [/*]

Quality of Life & Accessibility

  • The game will now detect if the player is using inverted mouse button settings and automatically adjusts in-game button prompts accordingly.

    [/*]

  • Added an option to toggle aiming down sights in Settings → Controls.

    [/*]

Jobs & Open World

  • Cyberpsycho Sighting: Bloody Ritual - the "Crack the ritualist's shard" objective now properly disappears from the Journal after completing the objective.

    [/*]

  • Sex on Wheels - now properly appears in the Journal after receiving the message from Jake Estevez.

    [/*]

  • Shot by Both Sides - fixed an issue where selecting a specific dialogue option in the conversation with Bree created a nameless, iconless item in the player's Inventory.

    [/*]

  • Shot by Both Sides - fixed an issue where the button to go to the lower level didn't appear on the elevator panel.

    [/*]

Gameplay

  • Fixed an issue where, when using a controller in Trauma Drama, the controllable character would default to shooting upwards instead of forward.

    [/*]

  • Players can now drop more Cyberware Capacity Shards if some within the intended drop limit were previously missed.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue causing automatic weapons to fire slower than intended.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where the Official BARGHEST Tac Vest didn't drop from the scripted Airdrop as intended.

    [/*]

  • The level 60 Engineer perk no longer activates the EMP blast outside of combat or after entering a vehicle.

    [/*]

  • Added an option to replay the gameplay tutorial at any time via Settings → Controls.

    [/*]

Miscellaneous

  • Added an option to tell Johnny to go away after you look at him for a short while when he appears in the passenger seat. He takes the hint and disappears as a passenger for a couple days.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where the sound of V's Radioport could be randomly interrupted by the Radioports of nearby NPCs.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where History by Gazelle Twin and Trash Generation played too loudly compared to other songs on the radio.

    [/*]

  • Improved the HDR Setting screen: fixed the HDR calibration preview so it correctly reflects the chosen settings, and clarified the description of the "Tone-Mapping Midpoint" setting.

    [/*]

  • Updated the End User Licence Agreement. You will be asked to accept it again when you load the game after updating.

    [/*]

  • Fixed several visual issues with missing, clipping, or floating textures.

    [/*]

  • Fixed several localization issues in various languages.

    [/*]

PC-specific

  • Added support for AMD FidelityFX Super Resolution 4 for compatible AMD GPUs. IMPORTANT: The FSR 4 option will not be available in the in-game settings until the supporting AMD driver is installed. Please note that the driver will be released at a later date.

    [/*]

  • Added support for AMD FidelityFX Super Resolution Frame Generation 3.1 for compatible hardware. It can now be used in combination with any upscaler.

    [/*]

  • Added support for ​Intel XeSS 2.0, with XeSS Frame Generation available on compatible hardware.

    [/*]

  • Added support for HDR10+ GAMING certified Intel GPUs. To enable this feature, your display must support the technology (find my display) and have "Game Mode" enabled. The HDR10+ GAMING toggle can be found in Settings in the Video tab.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where the DLSS Super Resolution Preset would invisibly revert from the CNN model to the Transformer model after restarting the game, even though the UI still displayed the CNN model as active.

    [/*]

  • Added more detailed information to the DLSS Super Resolution Preset tooltip in Settings to help players choose the best option for their setup.

    [/*]

  • Added the ability to move the mouse cursor to a different display while in Windowed Borderless mode.

    [/*]

  • Increased the maximum save size from 12 MB to 15 MB.

    [/*]

  • It will now be possible to rebind the key used to jump out of vehicles with the Stuntjock perk.

    [/*]
